title: Safe Variant Release Mesh: telemetry-driven cohort gating and automated rollback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a telemetry-driven mesh for safely releasing variant builds (model runtime, API surface, and config flips) using cohorted traffic ramps, feature flags, and automated rollback. This ticket covers policy design, enforcement components, dashboarding, and runbook automation for staged promotions across LTS and non-LTS channels.
goals: Provide a small-surface, reusable release mesh that can safely advance traffic percentages based on observed health signals
Enable automated rollback when fidelity or reliability regressions are detected without manual intervention
Standardize hold times, ramp steps, and metric thresholds across runtime and API releases to reduce operator cognitive load
Integrate with existing flagging system and telemetry (Prometheus + Honeycomb + SLO backend) and surface decisions in Console
non_goals: Full rewrite of rollout UI in Console (we will add hooks and telemetry only)
Address model output quality regression detection beyond existing Eval/QA pipelines (we will integrate signals but not build new eval infra here)
acceptance_criteria: A deployment can be promoted via a release-policy that specifies ramp steps and metric gates
At least three independent health signals (5xx error rate, request P95 latency delta, and tail CPU/GPU saturation) are evaluated in each gate
Gate evaluation runs on a sliding 5-minute window with a minimum sample size check
Automatic rollback is triggered if any gate violates the configured thresholds for two consecutive evaluation windows
Operators can override automation to pause or force-promote with an audit trail
Console shows per-release gate status, decisions, and metric deltas (links to dashboards)
Integration tests simulate a failing canary and assert rollback occurs within configured timeout
design_notes: Release mesh concept: central coordinator service (release-controller) receives release manifests and controls percentage routing via Flag API + Traffic Router
Gate evaluator calculates a composite health score from weighted metrics; each metric has tunable weight and threshold
Evaluation window: 5m sliding window, min 500 requests or minimum cohort duration of 10m before evaluating small cohorts
Rollback policy: immediate rollback to previous stable variant if composite health score crosses 'critical' threshold or if any single metric is above its 'hard' threshold
Soft vs hard thresholds: soft violations pause the ramp and create an operator alert; hard violations trigger auto-rollback
Safety net: shadow traffic and canary-only paths supported to test without customer impact
Audit: every decision stored as an event (release-id, gate-id, metric snapshot, decision, actor) forwarded to event-store and surfaced for postmortems
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Policy & evaluator library (2 wks) - implement gate DSL, composite scoring, unit tests
Phase 2: Controller + Router integration (3 wks) - controller drives Flag API, routes % via traffic router, enforces holds
Phase 3: Telemetry adapters (2 wks) - Prometheus/Honeycomb adapters, sample-size checks, SLO hook
Phase 4: Console hooks & dashboards (2 wks) - add gate status card, event timeline, links to dashboards
Phase 5: Chaos & integration testing (1 wk) - simulate failures and validate rollback and operator flows
Phase 6: Gradual rollout to internal teams and then external LTS customers (2 wks)
testing_plan: Unit tests for gate DSL and composite scoring edge cases
Integration tests: mocked telemetry producing healthy and failing signals to validate pause and auto-rollback
E2E test: deploy a canary with synthetic traffic generator that models production RT distribution
Load test: validate controller scales to 2000 concurrent releases with mocked metric backends
Security review: ensure audit trail cannot be tampered and RBAC prevents unauthorized force-promote
runbook: If a gate pauses: check gate timeline in Console -> examine per-metric deltas and underlying traces in Honeycomb
If auto-rollback fires: notify on-call via PagerDuty, open incident ticket, identify root cause via logs and recent changes
To force-promote: require two approvers and an explicit audit comment; only allowed if release-policy permits override
To abort a release: controller will set flag to previous stable reference and notify stakeholders; investigate before reattempt
Postmortem: capture event timeline, decision rationale, and required mitigations into Confluence (link in related_links)
